sections.h2: Where is Williamsburg County, SC, and what is in it?
sections.html:
Williamsburg County sits in the Pee Dee part of South Carolina and covers about 937 square miles, almost all of it land. Its neighbors are Florence and Marion counties to the north and northeast, Georgetown County to the east, Berkeley County to the south and Clarendon County to the west (Wikipedia).

Kingstree is the county seat and the largest community. The other towns are Andrews, which lies mostly in Georgetown County, plus Greeleyville, Hemingway, Lane and Stuckey. About 83 percent of residents live in rural areas, so many sellers here own a house on a larger lot, a family farm parcel or a mobile home on land.

The 2020 census counted 31,026 people, down from 37,217 in 2000. Kingstree itself had 3,244 residents in 2020 and covers roughly 3.2 square miles.

  • County seat: Kingstree, elevation about 59 feet
  • Population trend: falling since the 2000 census

sections.h2: What local history shows up in Williamsburg County property records?
sections.html:
The county was founded in 1785 and took its present shape in 1804, and the old courthouse in Kingstree dates to 1823, designed by Robert Mills (Wikipedia, Kingstree).

Thorntree, built in 1749, is described as the oldest home in the South Carolina lowcountry and was moved inside Kingstree for protection. The Kingstree Historic District and several individual houses are on the National Register of Historic Places.

If you are selling a Williamsburg County house that was never retitled after a parent died, expect the closing attorney to ask for estate paperwork before the deed can be recorded.

sections.html:
Manufacturing is the largest source of local jobs, followed by public administration, retail and health care. The table shows the figures reported for the county.

sections.h2: Which Williamsburg County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Four offices touch your tax bill: the assessor sets the value, the auditor applies the millage, the treasurer collects, and the delinquent tax office takes over after March 16. The South Carolina Association of Counties directory lists the contacts below (directory).

The treasurer and the delinquent tax office both list 201 W Main Street, Kingstree, as their physical address, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. except holidays (treasurer page). The delinquent office says it does not take American Express or Discover and does not accept payment on bills that are not yet delinquent.

We could not open a county page for the Register of Deeds, so we are not listing a phone or address for it. Ask the treasurer's office or your closing attorney where deeds are recorded.

sections.h2: When is Williamsburg County property tax due, and what does a late bill cost?
sections.html:
Real property tax is payable until January 15 without penalty, and the first penalty is 3 percent after that date. The county treasurer page and the state code describe the same ladder, with one difference in how the last step is worded.

  • Through January 15: no penalty.
  • After January 15: a 3 percent penalty.
  • February 2 through March 16: an added 7 percent penalty.
  • March 17: unpaid real property, mobile home and similar bills go into execution at the delinquent tax collector's office.

The state statute, S.C. Code 12-45-180, also lists a further 5 percent penalty if tax is still unpaid as of March 17. The county page we opened did not mention it, so ask the delinquent office for a payoff figure that includes every penalty and cost before you rely on any number.

Under the statute, the 3 percent step starts on the later of January 16 or thirty days after tax notices are mailed (S.C. Code Title 12, Chapter 45). That matters in a year when notices go out late.

sections.h2: How is a Williamsburg County house assessed, and how do you appeal?
sections.html:
South Carolina taxes an owner-occupied legal residence on 4 percent of fair market value and most other real property on 6 percent (S.C. Code 12-43-220). A rental house or a vacant lot is normally in the 6 percent group, so an heir who inherits a house and moves out may see the bill rise.

Counties reappraise on a five-year cycle, and a county may delay the new values by one tax year by ordinance. An owner must be told of a change of $1,000 or more. The county site posts a homestead exemption application, though we could not open the exemptions page, so ask the auditor which exemptions you qualify for.

The appeal path in Chapter 60 has several short clocks:

  • 90 days from the date the assessor mails the notice to file a written objection.
  • 30 days after the assessor's conference to file a written protest.
  • 30 days after the assessor's response to appeal to the county board of assessment appeals.
  • 30 days after the board's written decision to ask the Administrative Law Court for a hearing.

The statute text is at Chapter 60. In a year with no assessment notice, an owner can still object in writing, and an objection filed before the first penalty date applies to that year.

sections.h2: What happens if Williamsburg County property tax stays unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax leads to a delinquent notice, a levy by certified mail and a newspaper-advertised tax sale, but the owner keeps the right to redeem for twelve months after the sale. The steps come from S.C. Code Chapter 51 (text here).

  • On or about April 1, the officer mails a delinquent notice to the taxpayer and any grantee of record.
  • If the tax is still unpaid 30 days later, the officer takes possession of real property by certified mail.
  • The property is advertised as a Delinquent Tax Sale once a week for three weeks.
  • After a sale, the owner, a grantee, or a mortgage or judgment creditor may redeem within twelve months.
  • Redemption interest is a share of the bid: 3 percent in the first three months, then 6, 9 and 12 percent in later quarters.
  • The collector must send a certified notice 20 to 45 days before the redemption period ends.

The Williamsburg County delinquent tax page does not post sale dates or fee amounts in the text we could read, so call ext. 5800 for the current schedule.

sections.h2: What does a deed transfer cost in South Carolina?
sections.html:
The state deed recording fee is $1.85 for each $500 of value or fraction of it, and the seller is generally the party liable (S.C. Code Chapter 24). Of that amount, $1.30 goes to the state and $0.55 to the county.

The clerk or register of deeds must also receive an affidavit stating the value of the property, or the reason a deed is exempt. Transfers of $100 or less and deeds in lieu of foreclosure are among the listed exemptions. A false affidavit is a misdemeanor.

sections.h2: How do storms and the Black River affect a Williamsburg County house?
sections.html:
Low ground near the Black River can take on water in a major storm, and sellers should check the flood zone before listing. The river runs about 150 miles through Williamsburg, Clarendon, Sumter and Georgetown counties, and a 75-mile stretch joined the state Scenic River Program in 2001.

During Hurricane Matthew in October 2016, the National Weather Service reported storm-total rain in Williamsburg County approaching 10 inches by the morning of October 8, and a gauge northwest of Kingstree recorded 13.70 inches (NWS Wilmington).

A house with storm damage can be hard to finance with a standard loan, so a cash purchase as-is is one route for owners who cannot fund repairs.

sections.h2: What can you do if you want to sell a Williamsburg County house with tax due?
sections.html:
You can sell before a tax sale and have the unpaid tax paid from the sale proceeds at closing. The closing attorney requests a payoff from the treasurer or delinquent office and subtracts it from your proceeds.

  • Get a written payoff that includes penalties and costs, and ask how long it stays valid.
  • If the house was inherited, gather the death certificate and any probate papers.
  • Tell the buyer about any mobile home on the land, since mobile home tax is billed on the same ladder.
  • If a tax sale has already happened, count the twelve-month redemption window from the sale date.

This page is general information. The offices above set the actual amounts, and a South Carolina attorney can advise on your title.

faqs.q: What is the Williamsburg County property tax due date?
faqs.a: Real property tax in Williamsburg County is due on or before January 15 without penalty. A 3 percent penalty applies after that date, and a further 7 percent applies from February 2 through March 16, per the county treasurer page.

faqs.q: Who do I call about Williamsburg County property tax?
faqs.a: Call the county switchboard at (843) 355-9321 and use extension 5900 for the treasurer, 5600 for the auditor, 5500 for the assessor or 5800 for the delinquent tax collector. These numbers come from the South Carolina Association of Counties directory.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Williamsburg County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 90 days from the date the assessor mails the notice to file a written objection. After that, shorter 30 day deadlines apply at each later stage under S.C. Code Chapter 60.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Williamsburg County house if the tax is delinquent?
faqs.a: Yes, you can sell, and the unpaid tax is normally paid from the sale proceeds at closing. Ask the delinquent tax office for a written payoff first so the number includes penalties and costs.

faqs.q: Can I get my house back after a Williamsburg County tax sale?
faqs.a: Yes, for a limited time. The owner, a grantee, or a mortgage or judgment creditor may redeem real property within twelve months of the sale by paying the bid plus interest of 3, 6, 9 or 12 percent depending on the quarter.
